I farm only 8 mu, but I have 45 years of experience and well irrigation, so I will keep the full wheat-maize rotation on all of it. Since my household is small and some labor is off-farm, I will keep the plan simple, stable, and input-efficient rather than chasing extremes. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put enough nitrogen to secure tillering and grain filling, and rely on two irrigations because water is available and spring drought is a real risk here. For maize, I will use a hybrid because I want stable yield on limited land, and I will keep fertilizer moderate but sufficient, with two irrigations if rainfall is not enough. I will avoid unnecessary field operations, so I will use rotary tillage before wheat and no-tillage for summer maize after wheat harvest to save labor and time. I will also keep pesticide use to a practical level, applying only enough to control the usual weeds, diseases, and insects so the crop can finish well.
